content: Sugarcane is scientifically classified as Saccharum officinarum.

Sugarcane is grown chiefly in the main season (December - May) across the entire State: Early (Dec - Jan), Mid (Feb - March), and Late (April - May). It is also raised during a special season (June - September, planting in June - July) in parts of Tiruchirapalli, Perambalur, Karur, Salem, Namakkal, and Coimbatore districts. Early season varieties are suitable for the special season.

Key recommended varieties include: Co 86032 (performs in all soils, high yield, multi-ratooning, year-round planting, self-detrashing), CoV 92102 (non-flowering, performs in red, clay and alkaline soils), CoSi 95071 (performs well in Dec-Feb planting), CoC 90063 (drought and alkaline tolerant, non-lodging), Co 85019 and Co 86249 (drought tolerant, red rot resistant), Co Si(Sc)6, Co C (Sc)22, CoC (SC) 23, and CoC (SC) 24 (moderately resistant to red rot and drought tolerant), TNAU SC Si7 and TNAU SC Si 8 (drought/saline tolerant, red rot moderately resistant).

In wetlands (heavy soils), after harvest of paddy, form irrigation and drainage channels of 40 cm depth and 30 cm width at 6 m intervals across the field and along borders. Form ridges and furrows with 80 cm row spacing using a spade. Stir furrows with hand hoes and allow the soil to weather for 4 to 5 days.
In problem soils with excessive moisture where drainage is difficult, form raised beds at 30 cm intervals with a length of 5 m, width of 80 cm, and height of 15 cm.

In medium and light soil garden lands: perform initial ploughing with a two-disc plough followed by an eight-disc plough, use a cultivator for deep ploughing, and operate a rotovator once to pulverize the soil to a fine tilth. Level the field, open ridges and furrows 80 cm apart to a depth of 20 cm using a victory plough or tractor-drawn ridger, and open irrigation channels at 10 m intervals.
Apply FYM at 12.5 t/ha or compost at 25 t/ha or filter press mud at 37.5 t/ha before the last ploughing under garden land conditions. In wetlands, apply along the furrows and incorporate well.

Spread cane trash to 15 cm thickness over a 7 m x 3 m area, add pressmud 5 cm thick, and sprinkle a fertilizer mixture of mussoorie rock phosphate, gypsum, and urea (2:2:1 ratio) at 5 kg/100 kg trash. Moisten with water or cowdung slurry. Repeat layers up to 1.5 m height, cover with soil and pressmud (1:1 ratio) 15 cm thick, and leave for 3 months (moistening every 15 days except during rain). Turn and mix at 3 months and 4 months, maintaining moisture every 15 days during the 4th and 5th month.

If soil test is not done, apply blanket recommendation of NPK @ 300:100:200 kg/ha. Apply super phosphate (625 kg/ha) along furrows and incorporate with a hand hoe. Apply 37.5 kg Zinc sulphate/ha and 100 kg Ferrous sulphate/ha to zinc and iron deficient soils. Apply sulphur as Gypsum @ 500 kg/ha to sulphur deficient soils.

Take seed material from a short crop (6 to 7 months age) free from pests and diseases. Detrash cane by hand before sett preparation. Use a sharp knife or TNAU sett cutting machine to prevent splits. Discard setts with damaged buds, sprouted buds, or splits.
Treat setts with Azospirillum by preparing a slurry using 10 packets (2000 g)/ha of Azospirillum inoculum in water, and soak setts in the slurry for 15 minutes before planting.
Soak healthy setts for 15 minutes in 100 litres of water dissolved with 50 g Carbendazim, 200 ml Malathion, and 1 kg Urea.
Treat setts with aerated steam at 50°C for one hour to control primary infection of grassy shoot disease.
The recommended seed rate is 75,000 two-budded setts per hectare.

In wetlands, irrigate furrows to form slurry before planting; in dry/garden lands, arrange setts in furrows, cover with soil, then irrigate. Place setts along furrow center accommodating 12 buds/metre length, orienting buds laterally and pressing gently beneath soil while avoiding sunlight exposure. Plant extra setts near channels or use double-row planting at every 10th row for later gap filling.

Main season runs December - May throughout Tamil Nadu: Early (Dec - Jan), Mid (Feb - March), Late (April - May). Special season is June - September (planting period June - July) in parts of Tiruchirapalli, Perambalur, Karur, Salem, Namakkal, and Coimbatore districts. Early season varieties are suitable for the special season.

Key varieties released for productivity include: Co 86032 (performs well in all soils, extremely well in garden land, multi-ratooning, self-detrashing, wide row spacing amenable); CoV 92102 (non-flowering, self-stripping, suited for red, clay, and alkaline soils); CoSi 95071 (performs well in Dec-Feb planting); CoC 90063 (non-lodging, drought and alkaline tolerant); Co 86027 (mid-late planting, non-lodging, non-flowering); CoV 94101 (early planting, non-lodging, thick cane); Co 85019 (drought tolerant, red rot resistant); Co 86249 (red rot resistant, drought tolerant); Co Si(Sc)6 (drought tolerant, moderately red rot resistant); Co G (Sc)5 (suited for jaggery and tannery effluent soils); Co C (Sc)22 (drought tolerant, moderately red rot resistant); CoC (SC) 23 (moderately red rot resistant); CoC (SC) 24 (drought and saline tolerant, moderately red rot resistant); TNAU SC Si7 (drought and saline tolerant, moderately red rot resistant); TNAU SC Si 8 (tolerant to drought, waterlogging, and problem soils, moderately red rot resistant, suited for mechanized cultivation).

In wetlands (heavy soils) where preparatory ploughing to fine tilth is not possible after paddy harvest: form irrigation and drainage channels of 40 cm depth and 30 cm width at intervals of 6 m across the field and along borders. Form ridges and furrows at 80 cm spacing between rows using a spade. Stir furrows with hand hoes and allow soil to weather for 4 to 5 days.

subtopic: field preparation - problem soils with excessive moisture
content: In problem soils with excessive moisture where drainage is difficult, form raised beds at 30 cm intervals with dimensions: Length 5 m, Width 80 cm, and Height 15 cm.

In medium and light soils under flow or lift irrigation: initial ploughing with a two-disc plough followed by an eight-disc plough, deep ploughing with a cultivator, followed by rotovator operation to pulverize soil to a fine tilth free of weeds and stubbles. Level field, open ridges and furrows 80 cm apart and 20 cm deep using a victory plough or tractor-drawn ridger, and open irrigation channels at 10 m intervals.
Apply FYM at 12.5 t/ha or compost at 25 t/ha or filter press mud at 37.5 t/ha before the last ploughing under garden land conditions. In wetlands, apply along the furrows and incorporate well.

Spread cane trash to 15 cm thickness over a 7 m x 3 m area, add pressmud to 5 cm thickness, and sprinkle a fertilizer mixture of mussoorie rock phosphate, gypsum, and urea (2:2:1 ratio) at 5 kg/100 kg trash. Moisten with water or cowdung slurry. Repeat layers up to 1.5 m height, then cover with a 15 cm layer of soil and pressmud (1:1). Decompose for 3 months, moistening every 15 days (avoid in rainy season). Turn and mix at 3 months and leave for 1 month, then turn again at end of 4th month; moisten every 15 days during 4th and 5th months.

If soil test is not conducted, apply blanket NPK recommendation of 300:100:200 kg/ha. Apply super phosphate at 625 kg/ha along furrows and incorporate with a hand hoe. Apply 37.5 kg Zinc sulphate/ha and 100 kg Ferrous sulphate/ha to zinc and iron deficient soils. Apply sulphur as Gypsum @ 500 kg/ha to sulphur deficient soils.

Use seed material from a 6 to 7 month old short crop free of pests and diseases. Detrash canes by hand. Use a sharp knife or TNAU sett cutting machine to prevent splits. Discard setts with damaged buds, sprouted buds, or splits. For Azospirillum treatment, prepare slurry with 10 packets (2000 g)/ha of Azospirillum inoculum with sufficient water and soak setts for 15 minutes before planting.

Soak healthy setts for 15 minutes in 100 litres of water dissolved with 50 g Carbendazim, 200 ml malathion, and 1 kg urea. Treat setts with aerated steam at 50°C for one hour to control primary infection of grassy shoot disease.
Recommended seed rate is 75,000 two-budded setts per hectare.

In wetland heavy soils, irrigate furrows to form slurry, place setts along the centre of furrows accommodating 12 buds per metre length, orient buds laterally, and press gently into the soil avoiding sunlight exposure. Plant extra setts near channels or double-row plant every 10th row for later gap filling. In dry/garden land, follow the dry method: place setts along furrows, cover with soil, and then irrigate.
TNAU mechanical planter provides cost-effective planting with a saving of Rs. 3750/ha, can cover an area of 1.5 ha/day, reduces human labour drudgery, and lowers seed rate up to 5 tonnes/ha.

Paired row system of planting double side planting of sugarcane setts with 150 + 30 cm spacing for Astraf 8000 series (mechanical harvester) operated areas, and 150 + 30 cm spacing for New Holland 4000 series operated areas with a single row of cane planting. Alternatively, adopt a four feet row with two line planting in each row.
Under subsurface drip system, laterals may be placed at 20 cm depth in the furrows and setts are placed 5 cm above the laterals.
In Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative (SSI) system, transplant young chip bud seedlings raised in portray (25-35 days old) at wide spacing (5x2 feet) in the main field with a drip fertigation system.
Plant setts on one side of the ridge for 80 cm spacing in heavy soil to avoid sett rot and achieve better germination.

Intercropping Daincha / Sunhemp in wider spaced cane cultivated areas improves soil health, reduces weed infestation, reduces early shoot borer incidences, and increases cane yield. Sow rhizobium treated green manure seeds @ 10 kg/ha on the opposite side of ridge at 10 cm spacing on or before 3 days after planting. Incorporate the green manure crop 50-60 days after planting in between inter-rows and give partial earthing up with recommended dose of N fertilizer on 90-100 days after planting.
Introduce power weeder with rotovator for weeding and earthing up with ridger to save labour cost and reduce human drudgery.

Fill gaps within 30 days after planting with sprouted setts, or gap fill with two-budded setts/polybag seedlings within 15 to 20 days after planting to maintain optimum plant stand. Maintain adequate moisture for 3 weeks for proper establishment of sprouted setts.

Mulch the ridges uniformly with cane trash to a thickness of 10 cm within a week after planting to tide over drought, conserve moisture, reduce weed population, and minimise shoot borer incidence. In heavy soil and wetland conditions, mulch after 21 days of planting. Avoid trash mulching in areas where incidence of termites is noticed.

In areas of adequate irrigation, sow one row of soybean, blackgram, or greengram along the centre of the ridge on the 3rd day of planting. Incorporating daincha or sunhemp along ridges on the 45th day during partial earthing up increases soil fertility and cane yield. Intercropping of Co.1 Soybean yields 800 kg/ha without adverse effects on cane yield.

Wherever weed menace is higher, carry out one line weeding along the crop row and spade digging of ridges on 30, 60, and 90 days after planting. If herbicide is not applied, work junior-hoe along ridges on 25, 55, and 85 days after planting, remove weeds along furrows with hand hoe, or operate power tiller fitted with tynes.

Spray Atrazine 2 kg or Oxyfluorfen 750 ml/ha mixed in 500-600 litres of water as pre-emergence herbicide on the 3rd day of planting using a deflector or fan type nozzle fitted with knapsack sprayer. Alternatively, pre-emergence application of atrazine @ 1.0 kg a.i./ha on 3 DAP followed by post-emergence directed application of glyphosate @ 1.0 lit/ha on 45 DAP with hood + one hand weeding on 90 DAP registers maximum cane yield.
If pre-emergence spray is not carried out, apply Gramoxone 1 litre + 2,4-D sodium salt 2.5 kg/ha in 600 litres of water on the 21st day of planting as post-emergence spray.

For parasitic weed Striga, apply post-emergence 2,4-D sodium salt in 500 litres of water/ha. Avoid 2,4-D spraying when neighbouring crop is cotton or bhendi. Direct spray of 20% urea can also be applied for Striga control.

To suppress nut sedges (Cyperus rotundus), make pre-plant application of glyphosate at 2.0 kg/ha along with 2% ammonium sulphate 21 days before planting, followed by post-emergence direct spraying of glyphosate at 2.0 kg/ha along with 2% ammonium sulphate with a special hood on 30 DAP.
For creeper weeds, spray post-emergence directed application of Fernoxone (2,4-D sodium salt) @ 2 g + 10 g of urea per litre of water directly over the creeper weeds.

Pre-emergence application of Thiobencarb @ 1.25 kg a.i./ha provides effective weed control under intercropping systems of sugarcane with soybean, blackgram, or groundnut without affecting cane yield and quality.
After application of the 3rd dose of fertilizer (90 days), work a victory plough along the ridges for earthing up. At 150 days after planting, earthing up may be done with a spade.
Remove dry cane leaves on the 150th and 210th day after planting to avoid borer infestation.
Perform double line propping with trash twist at the age of 210 days of the crop.

Apply 275 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in three equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 days in coastal and flow irrigated belts (assured water). In lift irrigation belts (water scarcity), apply 225 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in three equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 days. For jaggery areas, apply 175 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in three equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 days.

subtopic: nitrogen saving via neem cake blending
content: Apply 67.5 kg N/ha + 27.5 kg Neem Cake at 30 days and repeat on the 60th and 90th days. Powder the required neem cake, mix thoroughly with urea, and keep for 24 hours before application to save 75 kg N/ha.

Mix 12 packets (2400 g)/ha of Azospirillum inoculant or TNAU Biofert-1 with 25 kg FYM and 25 kg soil and apply near clumps on the 30th day. Repeat on the 60th day with 12 packets, and repeat on the other side of crop row on the 90th day (for lift irrigated belts).

For band placement, open deep furrows of 15 cm depth with hand hoes, place fertilisers in band form, and cover properly. For subsurface application, apply 255 kg N as urea along with potash at 15 cm depth by the side of the cane clump to save 20 kg N/ha without yield reduction.
All leaves exhibit a yellow-green colour and retardation of growth. Cane stalks are smaller in diameter with premature drying of older leaves. Roots attain greater length but are smaller in diameter.

Reduction in length of sugarcane stalks, tapering rapidly at growing points. Leaves appear greenish blue, narrow, and somewhat reduced in length. Tillering is reduced, shoot/root ratio decreases, and root development is restricted.

Depressed growth, yellowing and marginal drying of older leaves, and development of slender stalks. Lower older leaves develop orange-yellow colour with chlorotic spots that turn brown with dead centres. Reddish discoloration on epidermal cells of upper surfaces and midribs. Young leaves develop from a common point giving a 'Bunched top' appearance. Poor root growth with fewer root hairs.

Mild deficiency develops anthocyanin pigments in leaves, pronounced bleaching of green colour along major veins, and striped effect due to chlorophyll loss along veins. In acute cases, necrosis occurs and growth ceases at the growing point (meristem).

Symptoms appear in young leaves as pale stripes with scanty chlorophyll between parallel lines. In advanced stages, young leaves turn completely white, including the veins. Root growth becomes restricted.
Depressed growth, development of distorted and chlorotic leaves, and definite leaf and stalk lesions. In extreme cases, the plant dies.

Perianaickenpalayam series (Inceptisols) of Coimbatore and Erode: FN = 4.17 T - 1.09 SN - 1.11 ON; FP2O5 = 1.01 T - 2.56 SP - 1.01 OP; FK2O = 3.44 T - 0.84 SK - 1.03 OK. Gadillum series (Red laterite) of Cuddalore: FN = 4.06 T - 0.74 SN - 0.87 ON; FP2O5 = 0.71 T - 1.09 SP - 0.72 OP; FK2O = 2.67 T - 0.57 SK - 1.30 OK. Irugur series (Inceptisols) of Coimbatore, Erode, Trichy and Salem: FN = 3.42 T - 0.56 SN - 0.93 ON; FP2O5 = 1.15 T - 1.94 SP - 0.98 OP; FK2O = 3.16 T - 0.73 SK - 0.99 OK.

In zinc deficient soils, apply basal application of 37.5 kg/ha zinc sulphate. In crops showing deficiency symptoms, apply foliar spray of 0.5% zinc sulphate with 1% urea at 15-day intervals until symptoms disappear.

In iron deficient soils, apply basal application of 100 kg/ha ferrous sulphate. In crops showing deficiency symptoms, apply foliar spray of 1% ferrous sulphate with 1% urea at 15-day intervals until symptoms disappear.
In copper deficient soils, apply CuSO4 @ 5 kg/ha to soil, or apply foliar spray of 0.2% CuSO4 twice during early stage of crop growth.

Apply 50 kg/ha micronutrient mixture (20 kg Ferrous sulphate, 10 kg Manganese sulphate, 10 kg Zinc sulphate, 5 kg Copper sulphate, 5 kg Borax) mixed with 100 kg well-decomposed FYM as soil application prior to planting, or apply TNAU MN mixture @ 50 kg/ha as EFYM for higher cane yield.

Moisten with water or cowdung slurry, repeating until the heap reaches 1.5 m height. Cover with 15 cm of soil and pressmud (1:1 ratio). Moisten every 15 days (avoiding rain), turn and mix at 3 months and 4 months, and continue moistening during the 4th and 5th months.

Apply 37.5 kg Zinc sulphate/ha and 100 kg Ferrous sulphate/ha to zinc and iron-deficient soils, and gypsum @ 500 kg/ha to sulphur-deficient soils.

Avoid exposing setts to sunlight. In dry/garden lands, arrange setts in furrows, cover with soil, and irrigate. Plant extra setts near channels or as double rows every 10th row for gap filling. In heavy soil, plant setts on one side of the ridge at 80 cm spacing to avoid sett rot.

TNAU mechanical planter covers 1.5 ha/day, saving Rs. 3,750/ha and reducing seed rate up to 5 t/ha. Paired row planting adopts 150 + 30 cm spacing for mechanical harvester operated areas. Under subsurface drip, laterals are placed 20 cm deep in furrows and setts 5 cm above laterals. For SSI, transplant 25-35 day old chip bud seedlings from polybags at 5x2 feet spacing with drip fertigation.

Fill gaps within 15 to 20 days (or within 30 days) after planting using sprouted setts or polybag seedlings to maintain optimum plant stand. Maintain adequate moisture for 3 weeks for proper establishment.

Mulch ridges uniformly with cane trash to 10 cm thickness within a week after planting (or after 21 days in heavy soil/wetland conditions) to conserve moisture, reduce weeds, and minimize shoot borer incidence. Avoid trash mulching where termites are noticed.

Sow one row of soybean, blackgram, or greengram along ridge centres on the 3rd day after planting. Alternatively, sow Rhizobium-treated daincha or sunhemp seeds @ 10 kg/ha on the opposite side of the ridge at 10 cm spacing on or before 3 DAP; incorporate 45-60 DAP during partial earthing up to enhance soil fertility, reduce early shoot borer, and increase yield. Co.1 soybean yields 800 kg/ha.

subtopic: chemical weed control in pure crop
content: Spray Atrazine 2 kg or Oxyfluorfen 750 ml/ha in 600 litres of water as pre-emergence on the 3rd DAP with a deflector or fan nozzle. Pre-emergence Atrazine @ 1.0 kg a.i./ha on 3 DAP followed by directed post-emergence Glyphosate @ 1.0 L/ha on 45 DAP with a hood + one hand weeding at 90 DAP provides maximum yield. Alternatively, apply Gramoxone 1 L + 2,4-D sodium salt 2.5 kg/ha in 600 L water on the 21st DAP.

For parasitic Striga weed, apply 2,4-D sodium salt post-emergence in 500 L water/ha (avoid spraying near cotton or bhendi) or spray 20% urea directly. For nut sedge (Cyperus rotundus), apply Glyphosate @ 2.0 kg/ha + 2% ammonium sulphate 21 days before planting, followed by post-emergence directed Glyphosate @ 2.0 kg/ha + 2% ammonium sulphate with a hood at 30 DAP. For creeper weeds, apply directed Fernoxone (2,4-D sodium salt) @ 2 g + 10 g urea per litre of water.
Under intercropping systems with soybean, blackgram, or groundnut, apply Thiobencarb pre-emergence @ 1.25 kg a.i./ha for effective weed control without affecting cane yield or quality.

If no herbicides are used, work a junior-hoe along ridges on 25, 55, and 85 DAP, or perform line weeding and spade digging on 30, 60, and 90 DAP. Carry out partial earthing up with a victory plough after the 3rd fertilizer application (90 DAP), and complete final earthing up at 150 DAP using a spade.
Remove dry cane leaves on the 150th and 210th day to prevent borer infestation. Perform double-line propping using trash twists at 210 days after planting to prevent lodging.

In coastal and flow-irrigated belts, apply 275 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in 3 equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 DAP. In lift-irrigated belts, apply 225 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in 3 equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 DAP. For jaggery areas, apply 175 kg N and 112.5 kg K2O/ha in 3 equal splits at 30, 60, and 90 DAP.

To save nitrogen: 1) Apply neem cake blended urea (67.5 kg N + 27.5 kg powdered neem cake mixed 24 hours prior) at 30, 60, and 90 DAP to save 75 kg N/ha. 2) Mix 12 packets (2400 g)/ha Azospirillum or TNAU Biofert-1 with 25 kg FYM and 25 kg soil near clumps at 30, 60, and 90 DAP. 3) Apply 255 kg N as urea with potash placed in 15 cm deep furrows beside clumps to save 20 kg N/ha.

Apply 50 kg/ha of micronutrient mixture (20 kg Ferrous sulphate, 10 kg Manganese sulphate, 10 kg Zinc sulphate, 5 kg Copper sulphate, 5 kg Borax mixed with 100 kg FYM) or TNAU MN mixture @ 50 kg/ha as EFYM prior to planting. For foliar correction, spray 0.5% ZnSO4 + 1% urea for zinc deficiency, 1% FeSO4 + 1% urea for iron deficiency at 15-day intervals, or 0.2% CuSO4 twice early for copper deficiency (or 5 kg CuSO4/ha soil application).

Apply Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus (TNAU Biofert-I) or Phosphobacteria at 12 packets (2.4 kg)/ha into soil on the 30th, 60th, and 90th DAP followed by copious irrigation. Do not mix biofertilizers with chemical fertilizers. Chemical N can be reduced by 25% when biofertilizers are applied.

Irrigate at germination phase (0-35 days) with shallow wetting (2-3 cm) at short intervals, preferably with sprinklers. During tillering (36-100 days) and grand growth (101-270 days), irrigate at 0.75 IW/CPE ratio (every 8 days in sandy soil, 10 days in clay soil). During maturity (271 days to harvest), irrigate at 0.50 IW/CPE ratio (every 10 days in sandy soil, 14 days in clay soil).

Under paired row drip systems (30x30x30/150 cm spacing), apply basal P @ 62.5 kg/ha at planting. Inject N and K @ 275:112.5 kg/ha as urea and MOP through a Venturi assembly in 10-14 equal splits every 15 days from 15 DAP up to 150-210 DAP. Irrigate once every 3 days based on ET demand. Add 50% extra N and K in low to medium nutrient soils.

Dig 4,444 pits/ha with 1.5 x 1.5 m spacing (0.9 m diameter, 0.38 m depth). Fill 15 cm with compost and soil. Plant 32 single-budded setts circular fashion per pit, leaving 10 cm from pit edges. Partially earth up at 50-60 DAP and fully earth up at 90-100 DAP leaving a 2.5 cm depression. Apply 275:62.5:112.5 kg NPK/ha (basal P; N & K in 14 splits from 15 to 210 DAP) using 3.0 m lateral spacing and 8 LPH drippers per pit.

Under drought conditions: soak setts in lime solution (80 kg kiln lime in 400 L) for 1 hour; plant in 30 cm deep furrows; apply 25 t/ha coir waste basally; spray 2.5% urea and 2.5% potash at 15-day intervals during stress; spray Kaolin @ 60 g/L water; adopt alternate/skip furrow irrigation; apply an additional 125 kg MOP/ha at 120 DAP; and remove dry trash at the 5th month to use as mulch.

In saline soils, increase seed rate by 25% and adopt a modified trench planting system. Incorporate organic manures (pressmud 10-15 t/ha, FYM 25 t/ha) and in situ green manures. Increase nitrogen dose by 25% and top-dress N and K via pocket manuring. Suitable tolerant genotypes include Co 6806, Co 7219, Co 7717, Co 8208, Co 85004, Co 85019, Co 86032, and CoC 671.

Spray sodium metasilicate @ 4 kg/ha in 750 L water at 6 months after planting, repeating at 8 and 10 months as a cane ripener. Assess maturity using a hand refractometer brix survey; 18-20% brix and a top-to-bottom brix ratio of 1:1 indicates peak maturity for harvest. Harvest early varieties at 10-11 months and mid-season varieties at 11-12 months by cutting stalks to ground level.

Raise 6 to 7 months old nursery crop prior to main field planting: sow in June for Dec-Jan planting, July for Feb-Mar, August for Apr-May, and Dec-Apr for June-Sept planting. Do not detrash or prop nursery canes. Harvest at 6-7 months, avoid bud damage, remove trash by hand only when cutting setts, transport canes with trash intact, and top-dress 50 kg urea/ha one month before cutting.

Within 10 days of harvest, remove trash (do not burn), irrigate copiously, shave stubbles with sharp spades to 4-6 cm depth along ridges, and work a cooper plough to break compaction. Fill gaps within 30 days using sprouted stubbles or polybag seedlings. Apply basal organic manure, super phosphate, and 25% extra N at 5-7 days after ratooning. Spray 2.5 kg FeSO4/ha at 15 days (repeat twice at 15-day intervals if chlorotic, adding 2.5 kg urea in the final spray). Hoe and weed at 20 and 40-50 DAP, earth up partially at 50 DAP and finally at 90 DAP, detrash at 120 and 180 DAP, prop at 180 DAP, and harvest after 11 months.

Apply foliar sprays of TNAU Sugarcane Booster @ 1.0, 1.5, and 2 kg/acre dissolved in 200 litres of water at 45, 60, and 75 DAP respectively to improve cane growth, weight, internodal length, yield, sugar content, and drought tolerance.
Sugarcane belongs to Family Gramineae, Class Monocotyledons, Order Glumaceae, Sub-family Panicoidae, Tribe Andripogoneae, and Sub-tribe Saccharininea.

scientific_name: Saccharum officinarum, Saccharum barberi, Saccharum sinenses, Saccharum robustum, Saccharum spontaneum
content: Sugarcane originated in New Guinea around 6000 BC. Cultivated canes belong to two main groups: thin, hardy north Indian types (S. barberi) and Chinese types (S. sinenses), and thick, juicy noble canes (S. officinarum). S. officinarum originated along the Indo-Myanmar China border with New Guinea as the main centre of diversity, called 'noble canes' due to thick, juicy, low-fibred canes of high sucrose content. Wild canes include S. robustum (origin New Guinea) and S. spontaneum (origin subtropical India), which inhabit swamps, river banks, and water courses.

Sugarcane is a tall perennial tropical grass that tillers at the base to produce unbranched stems 2-8 m tall and around 5 cm in diameter. The plant consists of roots, stems, leaves, and inflorescences.

The root system is fibrous and consists of two types: 'sett roots' and 'shoot roots'. Sett roots are activated from root primordia at the base of cane joints when planted, emerge within 24 hours of planting, and are mostly temporary. Shoot roots arise from the root rings of the lower nodes of tillers 5-7 days after planting; these are permanent, thick, fleshy, white, less branched, and continually produced from tillers.

Sugarcane is propagated vegetatively from stem cuttings. The stem is roughly cylindrical and consists of nodes and internodes. A node consists of a lateral bud (situated in the axil of the leaf on alternate sides of the stalk), root primordia (arranged in rows at the lower side of the leaf scar), and a growth ring (immediately above each node, coated with a waxy layer). The top of the stem is poor in sucrose.

The leaf consists of a blade and a sheath separated by a leaf joint, attached alternately to nodes. The leaf sheath is tubular. The leaf blade is linear or lanceolate with a prominent midrib grooved on the upper surface. The ligule is a membranous ring with long hairs separating the blade and sheath. Auricles are scarious extensions of the leaf sheath.

The inflorescence (tassel or 'arrow') is a loose terminal panicle 25-50 cm long with a silky appearance due to rings of long hairs below each spikelet. Spikelet arrangement is racemose. Each tassel contains several thousand tiny flowers capable of producing one seed. Flowering usually occurs at 10-12 months of age, though some varieties do not flower.
Sugarcane is a tropical plant that also grows in sub-tropics. It is cultivated between latitudes 35° N and 35° S (or 36.7° N and 31.0° S), from sea level up to an altitude of 1000 m or slightly more.

A total rainfall between 1100 and 1500 mm is adequate, provided there is abundant rain during vegetative growth followed by a dry period for ripening. It can be grown in areas with rainfall as low as 500 mm. Rainfall above 1500 mm causes cane lodging.
Optimum temperature for cane growth and germination is 27° to 33°C (80 to 90°F). Temperatures below 27°C are injurious and reduce tillering, while temperatures above 38°C adversely affect sprouting.
Ideal temperatures for plant processes are: Carbon assimilation: 30°C; Sugar synthesis: 30°C; Sugar transport: 30-35°C; Tillering: 33.3-34.4°C; Shoot growth: 33°C; Root growth: 36°C.

High humidity (80-85%) favours rapid cane elongation during the grand growth period. A moderate humidity of 45-65% coupled with limited water supply is favourable during the ripening phase. Humidity above 40% combined with warm weather favours vegetative growth.
Sugarcane is a sun-loving plant where greater incident radiation favours higher sugar yields. About 7-9 hours of bright sunshine daily is highly useful for both active growth and ripening.
Severe cold weather inhibits bud sprouting in ratoons and arrests cane growth. At temperatures between -1°C and 2°C, cane leaves and meristem tissues are killed.
High-velocity winds exceeding 60 km/hr are harmful to grown-up canes, leading to cane breakage and lodging.

In Tamil Nadu, sugarcane is grown chiefly in the main season (December - May) across the entire state: Early (Dec - Jan), Mid (Feb - March), Late (April - May). In parts of Tiruchirapalli, Perambalur, Karur, Salem, Namakkal, and Coimbatore districts, it is also raised during the special season (June - September, planting in June - July) using early season varieties. Eksali season is throughout the year except June.

In Karnataka, sugarcane planting for the 12-month crop (Eksali) is done in December-February, for the 15 to 16 month crop (Preseasonal) in October-November, and for the 18-month crop (Adsali) in July-August.

In Kerala, the normal planting season is October-December. Delay in planting reduces cane yield, and planting should not be delayed beyond February in the plains. In hilly tracts under rainfed conditions, planting should be done after abatement of heavy rains.

Plough the field 2 to 4 times to a depth of 50-60 cm with a tractor-drawn disc plough or victory plough to bring the soil to a fine tilth.
Perform harrowing at a shallow depth of 12-15 cm using a disc harrow or rotavator to pulverize, smoothen, crush clods, and compact the soil to conserve moisture.
Level the field using a tractor-operated leveller to ensure a uniform crop stand and easy movement of irrigation water.
Form irrigation-cum-drainage channels along and across the slope of the field at 10-15 m intervals.

Apply FYM at 12.5 t/ha or compost at 25 t/ha or filter press mud at 37.5 t/ha before the last ploughing. Alternatively, apply compost made from sugarcane trash and pressmud at a 1:1 ratio (prepared with 15 cm cane trash, 5 cm pressmud, rock phosphate, gypsum, and urea in a 2:2:1 ratio, moistened with cow dung slurry or water, and matured for 3 months).

Apply P fertilizer based on soil test values, or apply superphosphate at 37.5 kg/ha along the furrows and incorporate with a hand hoe. Apply 37.5 kg Zinc sulphate/ha and 100 kg Ferrous sulphate/ha in zinc and iron deficient soils.

Apply basal manures in the furrow in bands or pits at transplanting sites and irrigate the furrow. Well-soak nursery beds to lift settlings without root damage, then transplant at 30-45 cm spacing. Plant an additional line in every 10th row for gap filling. Provide life irrigation on the 3rd or 4th day, and fill gaps after 10-15 days using settlings from the 10th row. Avoid this technique in dry weather.

Mulch ridges uniformly with cane trash to a thickness of 10 cm within a week after planting to tide over drought, conserve moisture, reduce weed population, and minimise shoot borer incidence. In heavy soil and wetland conditions, mulch after 21 days of planting. Avoid trash mulching in areas where termite incidence is noticed.

In Tamil Nadu, with adequate irrigation, sow one row of soybean, blackgram, or greengram along the centre of the ridge on the 3rd day of planting. Intercrop daincha or sunhemp along ridges and incorporate on the 45th day during partial earthing up to enhance soil fertility and cane yield. Intercropping Co.1 Soybean yields 800 kg/ha without affecting cane yield. In Kerala, intercrop with short-duration pulse crops. In Karnataka, intercrop with groundnut and pulses.
Sugarcane is grown in sequence under 2 to 3 years rotation after the harvest of cotton, rice, maize, toria, potato, or wheat.
Fill gaps within 30 days after planting using sprouted setts and maintain adequate moisture for 3 weeks for proper establishment.

Perform earthing up in two or three stages: partial earthing-up at 45 days after planting by placing soil around shoot bases; full earthing-up after 120 days at peak tillering by fully moving ridge soil to cane bases, converting furrows into ridges. Victory plough may be worked along ridges after 3rd fertilizer dose (90 days). Earthing up with a spade can also be done at 150 days after planting.

Apply Ethephon (ethrel) at 500 ppm to control flowering in profuse flowering varieties. Altering planting dates or adopting Adsali/special season planting (July to September) avoids flowering. Non-flowering varieties include Co 8021, Co 86032, Co 87025, Co 91010, Co 94005, and Co 94008.
Remove unwanted bottom dry and green leaves around 150 days after planting after cane formation, and repeat at bi-monthly intervals depending on labour availability.
Tie leaves together using bottom dry and green leaves at 210 days of crop age for each row or by tying two rows together to prevent cane lodging.

Remove water shoots (robust, fast-growing late tillers resulting from excess water, heavy/late manuring, or inadequate earthing up) whenever they appear, as they reduce juice quality and affect adjacent cane growth; they can be utilized as cattle feed.

Lightly spread 1 to 2 tonnes of green wild indigo plants per acre over planted fields immediately after planting to reduce evaporation, prolong irrigation intervals, and later incorporate into the soil.

In low rainfall areas, open shallow furrows (8-10 cm deep) at 75-90 cm distance using a local plough or cultivator. Plant three-budded setts end-to-end (one sett per 30 cm furrow length) under adequate field moisture. Provide two blind hoeings to replace insect-damaged setts, followed by 2 to 5 inter-row cultivations after germination, and optional earthing up during July-August to prevent lodging and improve drainage.

In moderate rainfall areas with drainage issues, make 'V' shaped furrows 80-100 cm apart and 20-25 cm deep. Place setts horizontally end-to-end (or eye-to-eye if stalk quality is poor and internodes are long), doubling setts at furrow ends to prevent gap effects. Carry out repeated inter-row cultivation to level the land by end of May or mid-June (first earthing) and transform furrows into ridges (second earthing).

Dig pits of 0.9-1.2 m diameter and 0.38-0.45 m depth at 1.5 x 1.5 m spacing (4,444 pits/ha). Fill pits to 15 cm with compost mixed with native soil. Plant 16 or 32 single-budded setts in a circular manner 10 cm from the pit edge and cover with soil. Perform partial earthing up at 50-60 DAP and full earthing up leaving a 2.5 cm depression at 90-100 DAP. Apply 275:62.5:112.5 kg NPK/ha (all P basal; N and K as urea and MOP via fertigation in 14 splits from 15 to 210 DAP). Drip system has 3.0 m lateral spacing with 8 mm micro tubes of 1.0 m length (one 8 LPH); irrigate daily or alternately.

Form broad furrows at 150 cm spacing and plant setts in two rows 30 cm apart in the middle of furrows to facilitate mechanization and increase yield (136.3 t/ha compared to 126.7 t/ha in single row). Variety Co 94005 recorded highest yield in plant crop and performed best in ratoon crops, followed by Co 91010.

Use single-eyed setts (direct or raised in polybags and transplanted after 50-55 days) requiring 750 kg - 1 MT seed/acre, saving 60-70% seed cost. Space rows 90 cm apart and settlings at 45-90 cm (or 30 cm between sets). Maintain extra stock in the nursery to replace failed settlings.

Raise seedlings in perforated 10x15 cm plastic bags filled with FYM or pressmud, soil, and sand in a 1:1:1 ratio to achieve 95-99% field establishment. Transplant into small pits dug at 45 cm spacing, place a small quantity of phosphatic fertilizer covered with soil, and plant settlings after clipping green leaves.

Chip buds with a nodal portion using a bud chipping machine, treat with fungicide, and raise in nursery beds or polybags with FYM/pressmud, soil, and sand (1:1:1). Seed requirement is 1 to 1.5 tonnes/ha, and remaining canes can be sent for milling.

Dissect apical meristem and inoculate on nutrient media (tiller production starts at ~45 days; millions produced in 7-8 months). Transplant hardened plantlets (98-100% field survival). Apply 16.5 kg granular lindane/ha to soil 15 days after transplanting followed by irrigation to prevent early shoot borer. If necessary, remove the main shoot at 35-40 DAP. Perform major earthing up at 90-100 DAP. Achieves a 1:25 multiplication ratio.

subtopic: special planting methods (Sablang, Rayungan, Distance, Tjeblock)
content: Sablang method involves detaching tillers from mother plants once rooted and transplanting. Rayungan method decapitates seed stalks 4-6 weeks before planting to develop lateral shoots which are cut and planted in trenches. Distance planting transplants top setts from nursery at 90x50 cm spacing. Tjeblock method cuts stalks at half length and plants vertically with one node buried under soil with irrigation and fertilization.

scientific_name: Cyperus rotundus, Cynodon dactylon, Sorghum halepense, Panicum spp, Dactyloctenium aegyptium, Imperata cylindrica, Striga asiatica, Chenopodium album, Convolvulus arvensis, Amaranthus viridis, Portulaca oleracea, Commelina benghalensis, Trianthema portulacastrum
content: Nearly 150 weed species infest sugarcane. Major weeds include sedges (Cyperus rotundus), grasses (Cynodon dactylon, Sorghum halepense, Panicum spp, Dactyloctenium aegyptium, Imperata cylindrica), and broad-leaved weeds (Striga asiatica, Chenopodium album, Convolvulus arvensis, Amaranthus viridis, Portulaca oleracea, Commelina benghalensis, Trianthema portulacastrum). Weeds restrict tillering and cause direct yield losses ranging from 11% to 74%.
The critical period of crop-weed competition in plant crop sugarcane is 60-120 days after planting. In ratoon sugarcane, the critical period is 30-50 days after ratoon initiation.

Mechanically perform 3-4 hoeings after every irrigation during tillering phase. Culturally, practice crop rotation with green manures or fodder sorghum; intercrop with mustard, potato, or wheat in autumn, or blackgram, greengram, or cowpea in spring; and apply trash mulching (10-12 cm thickness) between cane rows soon after emergence to suppress weeds and conserve soil moisture.

To manage Striga, intercrop with legumes (soybean, cowpea, groundnut); pull plants within 2-3 weeks of flowering and burn them; apply trash mulch at 5.0 t/ha at 90 DAP; or apply pre-emergence atrazine at 1.0 kg/ha + hand weeding at 45 DAP + earthing up at 60 DAP + post-emergence 2,4-D Na salt at 5 g/l (0.50%) + urea 20 g/l (2%) at 90 DAP. Alternatively, spray 2,4-D Na salt @ 1.25 kg/ha in 500 L water/ha (avoid near cotton/bhendi) or apply 20% urea as a direct spray.

subtopic: chemical weed management in plant crop
content: Apply pre-plant glyphosate at 2.0 kg/ha with 2% ammonium sulphate 21 days before planting. Spray pre-emergence atrazine at 2 kg/ha or oxyfluorfen at 750 ml/ha in 500 L water on the 3rd day of planting (or atrazine @ 2.5 kg/ha in 1000 L water on 3rd-4th DAP). For post-emergence control, spray Gramoxone 1.5 L + 2,4-D sodium salt 2.5 kg/ha in 500 L water on the 21st day. Spray Ethoxysulfuron @ 13 g/10 L water to control Cyperus spp. If no herbicide is applied, work junior-hoe on 25, 55, and 85 DAP along ridges and hand-hoe furrows.

subtopic: chemical weed management in ratoon and intercropping
content: In ratoon crops, obtain maximum yield with three hoeings at 30, 60, and 90 days after harvest, OR apply atrazine 2.0 kg/ha pre-emergence followed by 2,4-D 1.25 kg/ha post-emergence at 90 DAH and directed spray of glyphosate 1.0 kg/ha at 150 DAH. In intercropping systems, apply Thiobencarb @ 1.25 kg a.i./ha as pre-emergence.

subtopic: herbicide dosage based on soil texture
content: Pre-emergence herbicide dosages based on soil clay content (<20%, 21-30%, >30%): Atrazine 50 FW (2.0, 2.5, 3.0 kg/ha, 6-8 weeks control); Ametryn 80 WP (2.0, 2.5, 3.0 kg/ha, 6-8 weeks); Diuron 80 WP (2.0, 2.0, 2.5 kg/ha, 5-7 weeks); Metribuzin 70 WP (2.0, 2.5, 3.0 kg/ha, 10-12 weeks); Alachlor 48 EC (3.0, 3.0, 4.0 kg/ha, 6-8 weeks); Trifluralin 48 EC (1.5 kg/ha across all soils, 5-7 weeks); Pendimethalin 50 EC (1.5 kg/ha across all soils, 8-10 weeks); Terbacil (1.0, 1.2, 1.5 kg/ha); Diuron + 2,4-D (1.2 + 1.8 kg/ha); Atrazine + Dalapon (1.25 + 2.5 kg/ha). Post-emergence herbicides: 2,4-D Sodium salt 80 WSP (1.0, 1.2, 1.5 kg/ha, 5-6 weeks); Paraquat (2.0, 3.0, 4.0 kg/ha); Glyphosate 41 WSC (1.2, 1.5, 2.0 kg/ha, 8 weeks); MSMA/MAMA (4.0 kg/ha across all soils, 6 weeks).

For raising nursery crops, the soil should be free from problems such as alkalinity, salinity, and water logging. Adequate irrigation and good road facilities for quick transport are required. Seed plots should be distributed in different divisions/sections for easy distribution among progressive farmers. Primary nurseries should be located in factory farms, research station farms, or Government seed farms.

Ploughing and cultivation are essential to prepare a good seedbed. A higher amount of organic manure is advantageous for obtaining a vigorous nursery crop; apply 25 to 30 tonnes of FYM or cured press mud about 15 days before planting.
A slightly narrower spacing is advantageous to obtain a higher yield of setts in nursery crops. Maintain a spacing of 75 cm between rows.

Select seed material from a short crop (6 to 7 months or 6 to 8 months age) free from pests, diseases, and damaged buds. Seed cane must be free from aerial roots and splits. Harvest seed crop one day before planting for higher percentage and uniform germination. Avoid detrashing and propping during crop growth, but detrash the cane by hand at the time of sett preparation. Avoid bud damage while cutting setts. Change seed material after every 2 to 3 seasons. If mature cane must be used, the top one-third portion can be used satisfactorily.
Apply 125 kg Urea/ha and 125 kg MOP/ha to the nursery crop one month prior to harvest, and irrigate the crop well before harvest.
Prepare a slurry with 10 packets (2000 g/ha) of Azospirillum inoculum with sufficient water and soak the setts in the slurry for 15 minutes before planting.
Soak the setts in Carbendazim solution at 1 gram per 1 litre of water before planting.
Treat setts with aerated steam at 50 °C for one hour to control primary infection of grassy shoot disease.

Raise a 6 to 7 months old nursery crop prior to main field planting: raise nursery in June for December-January (early season) planting; in July for February-March (mid season) planting; in August for April-May (late season) planting; and in December-April for June-September (special season) planting.

When water is in short supply or the field is occupied, raise nursery in 10x15 cm polythene bags filled with a 1:1 soil and compost mixture arranged closely in an open space near a water source. Plant scooped buds at 1-2 cm depth, or insert cut single-bud pieces up to node level with buds just touching the soil. Irrigate bags twice a week; saplings are ready for planting in 60 days.

Ratooning constitutes around 50% of the total area under cane. Ratoon productivity increases with proper management involving timely agricultural operations, proper nutrition management, integrated pest management, and maintenance of adequate plant population.

Selection of suitable sugarcane varieties with good ratoonability includes early category varieties: Co 8013, Co 6907, Co 8014, 85A261, 87A298, 90A272, 92A123, 81V48, 91V83, 93V297, 97V60, and 83R23; and mid-late category varieties: 83V18, 89V74, 93A145, 94A109, Co 7219, Co 7805, Co 7706, and Co 86032.

subtopic: field preparation and stubble shaving for ratoon crop
content: At the time of harvest of plant crop, use sharp knives for cutting the clump to ground level. Clean field by removing dead canes, trash, etc. Break clods by intercultivation between furrows with the plough. Stubble shaving has to be done with sharp knives to the ground level to remove generated old buds and rejuvenate new buds, without disturbing the clump.

Fill gaps in ratoon crop to maintain millable cane numbers. This can be done by: placement of single/two/three budded setts in the gaps; pre-germinated settlings raised through polybag system; or taking clumps from thickly populated areas and filling the gaps.

Cut single budded setts carefully and plant in bags keeping bud in upward direction covered with a thin layer of soil medium. Keep bags in rows under shade, leaving a path every six rows for sprinkling water with rose cans. Buds sprout from 10th to 12th day. Use 35-40 day old settlings for planting. Make a gentle cut on one side of the bag along its length with a blade, remove bag carefully without disturbing soil, place setting in furrows of the main field and press gently.

Apply 3 tonnes of trash per hectare spread between furrows. Benefits include: soil cover, prevents moisture evaporation, conserves soil moisture, keeps root zone moist, helps produce more tillers, controls Early Shoot Borer (ESB), keeps standing crop lush green, and aids nutrient absorption.

subtopic: inorganic nutrient management for ratoon crop
content: Apply 3 bags of urea, 5 bags of super phosphate, and 1.50 bags of muriate of potash at the time of ratooning. Apply a second dose of 3 bags of urea at 45th day after ratooning.

subtopic: organic nutrient management for ratoon crop
content: Apply 2 bags of bio-compost, 4 kgs of Azospirillum, and 4 kgs of phosphobactor per acre for higher yields and better sugar recovery.

subtopic: chemical and manual weed control in ratoon crop
content: Do not apply pre-emergence weedicide (Atrozin) in ratoon crops. Use post-emergence weedicides Gramoxone at 4.50 liters and Femoxone at 2.50 Kg per hectare for weed control. One manual weeding may be done if necessary.

Ratoon crops normally require 18-20 irrigations in their life span. Drip irrigation is recommended in places of water scarcity. Alternate furrow method is recommended in certain cases. Where plenty of water is available, normal irrigations at regular intervals are recommended for higher yields.

Ratoon crops mature early (at least by one month) compared to plant crop. Secure cutting orders from sugar factories well in advance so that cane may be used as open mill cane at the start of the crushing season.

Advantages of ratoon crop: No preparatory cultivation required; saving in cost of seed material; saving of labor on seed cane collection, sett cutting, and planting; fallen leaves/trash convert into organic matter; matures at least one month early; expenditure involved is less compared to plant crop.

subtopic: disadvantages and challenges of ratoon cropping
content: Disadvantages of ratoon crop: Cane yields are generally lower than plant crop; nitrogenous fertilizer requirement is higher; neglected cultivation makes crops more prone to pests and diseases; flowering in certain varieties under delay in harvest might result in increased fiber content affecting sugar recovery.

Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative (SSI) is an approach based on 'more with less' principles involving less seeds, less water, and optimum utilization of fertilizers and land to achieve higher yields. Key principles include raising nursery using single-budded chips, transplanting young seedlings (25-35 days old) after grading, wide spacing (5 x 2 ft), avoiding water inundation, encouraging organic nutrient management and plant protection, and intercropping. This results in at least 20-25 tillers/plant and 9-10 millable canes/plant.

Select healthy canes that are 7 to 9 months old with 10-12 buds per cane. Remove buds using a Bud Chipper. The chipped buds have to be treated with organic or chemical solutions. About 450-500 canes per acre are required.

Fill half of each cone in the tray with well-decomposed coco-pith. Place the buds flat or in a slightly slanting position and cover completely with coco-pith. Tightly cover and keep bundles in a shade net or inside a room to prevent water, air, or sunlight entry. If cold, provide artificial warmth using electric bulbs. Under warm conditions, white root primordia emerge in 3-5 days and shoots appear in the next 2-3 days.
Initiate watering in the evenings for 15 days using rose cans based on coco-pith moisture. Grading of seedlings should be done at the six-leaf stage (about 20 days old).

Clear preceding crop residues and collect/remove stubbles or incorporate residues into soil using a rotavator. Perform one or two initial ploughings using tractor-drawn implements and allow soil to weather for a week or two before further tillage operations.

Make furrows with a distance of 5 feet in between. Run a sub-soiler attached to the ridger/plough through the furrow to loosen the soil, facilitating manure incorporation, deep planting, and lodging prevention.

Transplant seedlings from the nursery to the main field at 25 to 35 days of age. Follow a zigzag method of planting with a plant-to-plant distance of 2 ft and row spacing of 5 ft to maximize space utilization, facilitate sunlight penetration, and promote profuse tillering. Seed requirement is reduced to 5,000 single-budded chips per acre.

Intercrop sugarcane with crops like wheat, potato, cowpea, french bean, chickpea, watermelon, and brinjal. Intercropping utilizes land effectively, provides additional income, and suppresses weed growth by up to 60%.

Maintain a weed-free environment through deep ploughing and removal of perennial weeds. Carry out hand weedings and mechanical weedings at 30, 60, and 90 days after planting for long-term weed control.
Apply trash mulch at 1.5 t/acre within 3 days of planting to check weeds and conserve moisture. Additionally, detrashed leaves can be spread as mulch in the interspaces.
Soil testing is recommended to assess nutrient requirements. If unavailable, apply NPK at the rate of 112 kg N, 25 kg P, and 48 kg K per acre through inorganic or organic methods.

Apply organic manure such as FYM, compost, or well-decomposed press mud at 8-10 tonnes/acre, adjusting quantities to supply 112 kg N/acre. Mix Trichoderma (1 kg/acre), Pseudomonas (1 kg/acre), and decomposing cultures with the organic manures to enhance soil fertility.

Irrigate once in 10 days during the tillering stage (36-100 days), once in 7 days during the grand growth period (101-270 days), and once in 15 days during the maturity period (from 271 days till harvest). Adjust frequency based on soil type (more frequent for sandy soil, less for clay soil).

Practice alternate furrow irrigation by first irrigating odd-numbered furrows, followed by even-numbered furrows after 7 to 15 days depending on crop age and soil moisture. This practice saves up to 50% water.

Compared to flood irrigation, drip fertigation in SSI reduces water requirement from 2200 mm to 1000 mm, lowers single-irrigation volume from 6.1 lakh litres to 0.4 lakh litres, and decreases irrigation interval from 7 days (36 irrigations total) to 1 day (250 irrigations total). It increases cane yield from 92-105 t/ha to 150-200 t/ha, doubles fertilizer use efficiency from 30% to 60%, and raises the benefit-cost ratio from 1.97 to 4.7.
Apply soil at the root zone to strengthen crop stand and prevent lodging. Typically, two earthing up operations (partial and full) are carried out during the crop duration.

Recommended Dose of Fertilizer (RDF) for SSI drip fertigation is 275:63:115 kg NPK/ha applied once every 10 days. The schedule is: 0-30 DAP: 39.4 kg N, 0 kg P, 0 kg K; 31-60 DAP: 48.6 kg N, 26.25 kg P, 9.0 kg K; 61-90 DAP: 51.4 kg N, 20.50 kg P, 13.5 kg K; 91-120 DAP: 55.2 kg N, 16.25 kg P, 14.6 kg K; 121-180 DAP: 57.8 kg N, 0 kg P, 40.5 kg K; 181-210 DAP: 10.5 kg N, 0 kg P, 35.0 kg K (Total: 275 kg N, 63 kg P, 115 kg K per ha).

Sucrose content reaches the desirable level at the 10th month of the one-year crop duration, making canes ready for harvest within the following two months. Harvesting is typically coordinated with sugar factory timings.

Water requirement varies depending upon agro-climatic conditions, soil type, planting methods, use of manures and fertilizers, and yield. Hot weather with dry winds and drought increases water requirement. Sowing in trenches needs less water, whereas sandy soils and higher fertilizer application increase water uptake. On average, 1 ton of cane needs about 60-70 tons of water. Thin cane varieties need 150 cm water, thick canes need 200 cm, and Adsali planted canes need 200 cm in addition to 75 cm rainfall. The crop should be irrigated when available water reaches 50% level.

Soil must have sufficient moisture at sowing. First irrigation should be done when about 20-25% of plants have germinated or about 20 days after sowing. Irrigations are given at 10-15 days interval during summer, 25-30 days interval during winter, and during rainy season as needed if drought occurs. Maximum water is required at tillering stage and during elongation or grand growth phase.

Under waterlogging conditions, root respiration becomes poor, nutrients are leached down, useful micro-organism activity is reduced, and the crop lodges with excessive branching, resulting in poor quality and very low yield. It is necessary to drain excess water from the field.
Average water requirement for sugarcane is 1800 to 2200 mm. For a 365-day crop duration, total water requirement is approximately 2000 mm, provided across 24 irrigations.

Water requirement by growth phase for a 12-month crop: Germination phase (0-45 days) requires 300 mm; Tillering phase (45-120 days) requires 550 mm; Grand growth phase (120-270 days) requires 1000 mm; Ripening phase (270-360 days) requires 650 mm.

Irrigation intervals based on soil texture and growth phase: Germination (0-45 days): 5-6 days in coarse textured soil, 6-7 days in medium textured soil, 8-10 days in fine textured soil. Tillering phase (45-120 days): 6-7 days in coarse textured soil, 7-10 days in medium textured soil, 12-15 days in fine textured soil. Grand growth phase (120-270 days): 7 days in coarse textured soil, 10 days in medium textured soil, 12-15 days in fine textured soil. Ripening phase (270-360 days): 10 days in coarse textured soil, 12-15 days in medium textured soil, 15-20 days in fine textured soil.

Water use efficiency comparison by irrigation system: Rain gun sprinkler uses 175.26 ha-cm water applied, gives cane yield of 126.56 mt/ha, water use efficiency of 0.72, and C.S. 17.87 mt/ha. Drip irrigation uses 132.14 ha-cm water applied, gives cane yield of 128.64 mt/ha, water use efficiency of 0.97, and C.S. 18.29 mt/ha. Furrow irrigation uses 258.45 ha-cm water applied, gives cane yield of 104.42 mt/ha, water use efficiency of 0.40, and C.S. 14.71 mt/ha.

Poor irrigation leads to decreased internode length, decreased juice amount, increased fiber percentage, decreased germination rate, and decreased sugar yield. Heavy irrigation leads to death of buds, damage to roots, decreased sugar content, decreased cane yield, and inability of plants to absorb elements from soil, causing yellowing.

Flood irrigation allows free flow of water in all directions, practiced in flat-planted cane, but results in high water loss. Furrow irrigation is most commonly used and effective for early plant crop; in later growth periods and ratoon crops, water distribution can become problematic due to furrow deterioration. Reduced furrow length can be used for better distribution in later stages.

Sugarcane is planted in flat beds, and after germination, 45 cm wide and 15 cm deep furrows are made in alternate inter-row spaces, resulting in considerable water savings. In autumn planting, 7 irrigations are given in plains (5 before rain and 2 after rain). In spring planting, 6 irrigations are given (4 before rain and 2 after rain), with one irrigation at tillering being mandatory.

Sprinkler irrigation utilizes hand and automatically moved spray guns, replacing cumbersome booms and hand-moved sprinkler laterals. Prevailing winds exceeding 4 to 5 m/sec limit sprinkler usefulness.

Drip irrigation applies water precisely, slowly, and frequently through point or line source emitters on or below the soil surface at operating pressure of 20-200 kPa and discharge rate of 0.6 to 20 LPH. 12 mm drip laterals are placed in the middle ridge of each furrow at 240 cm lateral spacing, with 8 LPH clog-free drippers spaced 75 cm apart on lateral lines. Lateral length should not exceed 30-40 m. Irrigation is given once in three days based on crop evapo-transpiration demand.

Surface drip applies water to
 soil surface as drops or streams via emitters; integral dripline is recommended for sugarcane. Subsurface Drip (SDI) applies water below the soil surface through emitters molded on the inner dripline wall (discharge 1.0-3.0 LPH), installed at predetermined depth based on soil type and crop requirements. SDI types include 'one crop' and 'multicrop'. SDI saves water and improves yields by eliminating surface evaporation and reducing weeds and disease incidence.

Drip design parameters: For Single row surface drip: distance between two paired rows/two rows is 1.2 to 1.5 m, distance between two driplines is 1.2 to 1.5 m, emitter distance is 0.4 to 0.6 m, discharge is 1.0 to 3.0 LPH. For Paired row surface drip: distance between two rows of a pair is 0.4 to 1.0 m, between two paired rows is 1.4 to 2.0 m, between two driplines is 1.8 to 2.5 m, emitter distance is 0.4 to 0.6 m, discharge is 1.0 to 3.0 LPH. For Paired row subsurface drip: distance between two rows of a pair is 0.4 to 1.0 m, between two paired rows is 1.4 to 2.0 m, between two driplines is 1.8 to 2.5 m, dripline installation depth is 0.15 to 0.30 m (15 to 30 cm), emitter distance is 0.4 to 0.6 m, discharge is 1.0 to 2.3 LPH.

Benefits of drip irrigation include saving 40-70% (or 25-50%) of irrigation water, reduced labor costs, 90% uniformity in water distribution, suitability for inferior quality or saline water, reduced irrigation period (2-3 hours), homogeneous plant growth, reduced evaporation losses, suitability for marginal and undulating lands, lower tillage requirements, reduced weeds and pest/disease infestation, increased planting area by eliminating field canals, and reduced human water-contact infections (bilharzia/schistosomiasis).

Recommended standard fertilizer dose is 275:62.5:112.5 kg NPK/ha, whereas recommended dose for fertigation is 275:15:112.5 kg NPK/ha. Nitrogen and Potassium @ 275 and 112.5 kg/ha may be applied in 14 equal splits at 15-day intervals starting from 15 DAP (delivering 25 kg N and 8 kg K2O per ha per split) using Urea and MOP (white potash). Fertigation up to 210 DAP is recommended. Delivery can be done via fertilizer tank, venturi system, injector pump, Non-Electric Proportional Liquid Dispenser (NEPLD), or automated systems.

Fertigation schedule by crop stage: First stage (planting to 70 days, every 5th day): 14 applications of 12-61-00 @ 0.9 kg/time, 13-00-45 @ 1.8 kg/time, and Urea @ 12.1 kg/time. Second stage (71 to 120 days): 10 applications of 12-61-00 @ 1.2 kg/time, 13-00-45 @ 5.0 kg/time, and Urea @ 20.9 kg/time. Third stage (121 to 160 days): 8 applications of 12-61-00 @ 3.1 kg/time, 13-00-45 @ 5.6 kg/time, and Urea @ 14.1 kg/time. Fourth stage (161 to 210 days): 10 applications of 12-61-00 @ 2.5 kg/time, 13-00-45 @ 6.8 kg/time, and Urea @ 8.3 kg/time.

Nutrient fertigation schedule (N, P2O5, K2O in kg/ha/day): For Seasonal (12 months)/Ratoon Sugarcane: 1-30 Days: 1.20 N, 0.10 P2O5, 0.20 K2O; 31-80 Days: 1.50 N, 0.40 P2O5, 0.24 K2O; 81-110 Days: 2.00 N, 1.00 P2O5, 0.40 K2O; 111-150 Days: 0.75 N, 0.30 P2O5, 0.75 K2O; 151-190 Days: 1.50 N. For Preseasonal (14 to 16 months) Sugarcane: 1-30 Days: 1.5 N, 0.15 P2O5, 0.25 K2O; 31-80 Days: 2.0 N, 0.60 P2O5, 0.30 K2O; 81-110 Days: 2.5 N, 1.50 P2O5, 0.50 K2O; 111-150 Days: 0.75 N, 0.50 P2O5, 1.0 K2O; 151-190 Days: 1.80 N.

Water-soluble fertilizers suitable for fertigation via drip irrigation: Nitrogen sources: Urea (46-0-0), Ammonium Nitrate (34-0-0), Ammonium Sulphate (21-0-0), Calcium Nitrate (16-0-0), Magnesium Nitrate (11-0-0), Urea Ammonium Nitrate (32-0-0), Potassium Nitrate (13-0-46), Monoammonium Phosphate (32-0-0). Phosphorus sources: Monoammonium Phosphate (12-61-0), Monopotassium Phosphate (0-54-32), Phosphoric Acid (0-82-0). Potassium sources: Potassium Chloride (0-0-60), Potassium Sulphate (0-0-50), Potassium Nitrate (13-0-46), Potassium Thiosulphate (0-0-25), Monopotassium Phosphate (0-52-34). NPK sources: Polyfeed (19-19-19 and 20-20-20). Micronutrients: Fe EDTA (13), Fe DTPA (12), Fe EDDHA (6), Zn EDTA (15), Ca EDTA (9.7), Rexolin CXK (B+Cu+Fe+Mn+Mo+Zn+Mg).

Drought occurs when evapotranspiration exceeds soil moisture supply. Sugarcane requires the most irrigation during germination and grand growth phase. In India, these critical stages coincide with summer months when water availability is poor, leading to crop drying and yield loss if water is insufficient.

Drought management cultural practices: Plant sugarcane in early season at 30 cm depth in furrows; in drought areas, plant setts at 60-75 cm spacing instead of 90 cm; soak setts in lime solution (80 kg kiln lime in 400 L water) for one hour; perform basal incorporation of coir waste @ 25 tonnes/ha during the last ploughing; remove dry trash at the 5th month and leave as field mulch to reduce soil temperature up to 2°C; adopt alternate furrow and skip furrow irrigation under water scarcity.

To mitigate moisture stress during drought periods: Spray potash and urea each at 25 g in 1 litre of water at 15-day intervals; spray Kaolin @ 60 g in 1 litre of water to alleviate water stress; apply an additional 125 kg of Muriate of Potash at 120 days after planting.
Drought tolerant and resistant varieties recommended for drought management in sugarcane are Co 86032, Co 99004, Co 94008, and Co 86249.
